**1. Bills not showing on TransUnion**
I can't tell from your profile whether something is broken. It shows Bill Reporting active since 2026-02-01, with 8 months reported for your phone, electric and internet. It doesn't show which bureaus get those bills or how long they take to appear, so I can't confirm that. Rent and bills may also be reported differently. Human support can check this for you.

**2. Your score going from 695 to 702**
I can't pinpoint the exact cause, and no one can promise what a score will do. Here is what in your profile may be helping (VantageScore 3.0):
- Utilization (how much of your card limits you're using) is 12%, with $300 on $2,500 in limits.
- Your recent payments were all on time, including rent, Credit Builder and the Secured Card.
- You have no negative items and no hard inquiries in the last 12 months.

**3. A missed final electric bill**
It does matter. I can't confirm how the app handles a final bill, but a utility company can send an unpaid bill to collections whether or not the app reports it.
- An accurate collection can stay on your report up to 7 years from the first missed payment.
- Paying it later doesn't remove it. It would show as paid.
- VantageScore 3.0 ignores paid collections. FICO 8 counts them unless the original balance was under $100. Lenders use different models.
- No one can promise it would come off.

The easier fix is to prevent it. Ask the utility for your final bill, confirm your forwarding address, and pay it before you move.

Next step: Ask support (Help > Chat with support) which bureaus receive your bill reports and what happens to them when you move.
improvements.candidate_reply:
**1. Rent on TransUnion, but not bills**

Nothing looks broken. Rent Reporting sends on-time rent to TransUnion and Experian. Bill Reporting sends your phone, electric, and internet payments only to Equifax. So you would not see them on TransUnion. Your profile shows all three bills active, with 8 months reported each. Check your Equifax report to see them.

**2. Your score going from 695 to 702**

I can't point to one sure cause. Your profile shows no negative items and no hard inquiries (credit checks from new applications) in the last 12 months. It does show on-time payments on the Secured Card, Credit Builder, and rent. Utilization (how much of your card limits you're using) is 12%, based on $300 in balances against $2,500 in limits. Small moves with no new negative item are normal. Lenders also report on different dates, so balances can shift from month to month.

**3. A missed final electric bill**

It can matter. The app never reports a late bill, but that doesn't stop your electric provider from sending an unpaid bill to a collection agency on its own. A collection can stay on your report for up to 7 years from the first missed payment.

If it did go to collections and you paid it, it would not be removed. A paid non-medical collection shows as paid. Some newer scoring models, like VantageScore 3.0 (the one your profile shows), ignore paid collections. Other models, like FICO 8, may still count it. No one can promise it would come off.

The simple fix is to pay the final bill before you move. Then it never gets the chance to go to collections.

Next step: Set a reminder now to pay your final electric bill on your move-out date.
